newsitem.title: UK: UK Japan stocks ease on followthrough, Toyota dips.
newsitem.headline: UK Japan stocks ease on followthrough, Toyota dips.

text.p: Japanese stocks traded here on Wednesday eased amid follow-through selling after steep falls in Tokyo on currency and interest rate concerns, dealers said.
Continuing fears of a hike in the official discount rate, the stronger yen and weaker-than-expected results from Toyota, released after the Japanese close, sent the London market lower.
The Nikkei 50 eased 0.41 points to 1,536.53 by 1357 GMT, having touched 1,534.22 and 1,536.95 during the session.
Toyota shares fell nearly 80 yen to 3,402.5 yen from a Tokyo close of 3,480 yen.
Shares in the carmaker, among other exporters, fell 100 yen in the Tokyo session due to the yen's renewed strength.

Toyota said 1996/97 profit grew 50 percent to 385.92 billion yen and forecast growth to 630 billion this year. However, analysts' forecasts were for more than the 733.80 billion, its highest ever level, achieved in 1989/90.
